t: The Russian fleet had sailed seven months and 18,000 nautical miles from the Baltic Sea, and it reached the strait with fouled hulls, crews with little training and a speed held to 9 knots by its slowest ships.
Japanese gunnery, high-explosive shells and wireless reports from scouting ships gave Tōgō the advantage, and four Russian battleships were sunk by sunset on 27 May.
Nearly the whole Russian fleet was sunk, captured or interned, and the Japanese lost three torpedo boats; the Treaty of Portsmouth followed in September 1905.
dyk: Oslyabya was the first modern armoured warship ever sunk by gunfire alone. One Japanese junior officer on the cruiser Nisshin, Takano Isoroku, lost two fingers in an accidental shell explosion and later became Admiral Yamamoto Isoroku.
ev: Japanese destroyers attack the Russian Far East Fleet at Port Arthur and the Russo-Japanese War begins
Rozhestvensky's squadron leaves Reval and Libau for the Far East, and the voyage takes it past the Dogger Bank, around Africa and on to Cam Ranh Bay
On 27 May the Japanese auxiliary cruiser Shinano Maru sights the Russian fleet and wireless reports reach Tōgō on the Mikasa
In the afternoon of 27 May Tōgō turns his line in sequence in the afternoon, Oslyabya, Knyaz Suvorov, Imperator Aleksandr III and Borodino are lost, and Rozhestvensky is knocked unconscious
From about 20:00 Japanese destroyers and torpedo boats attack the scattered Russian ships through the night
On 28 May Nebogatov surrenders his remaining battleships and Tōgō accepts after the signal flags are understood
The Treaty of Portsmouth ends the war
Britain begins construction of HMS Dreadnought

f.place: The Tsushima Strait, east of Tsushima Island, between the Japanese island of Kyushu and the Korean Peninsula
f.sides: The Japanese Combined Fleet under Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō, with over 40 vessels leading from the flagship Mikasa; the Russian Second Pacific Squadron under Admiral Zinovy Rozhestvensky, joined by the Third Pacific Squadron under Rear Admiral Nikolai Nebogatov, numbering 38 ships and outnumbered nearly three to one in total hulls
f.outcome: All 11 Russian battleships were lost, seven sunk and four captured. Russian dead were more than 5,000, and the Japanese lost no heavy ships and had 117 dead.
